\begin{abstract}
We give explicit arbitrary-order derivative enclosures for the central heat
kernel and its negative logarithm on $\SU$, regarded as the unit three-sphere
with heat generator $\tfrac12\Delta$.  Opposite Poisson images are paired
before division by the Weyl denominator.  On the identity chart this gives a
sharp exponentially small correction to the Gaussian action.  A second
majorant, obtained by maximizing each exponential--polynomial factor in heat
time, controls the transition chart without an order-dependent small-time
restriction.  At the cut locus we pair odd affine-Weyl images, prove an
explicit positive principal-pair lower bound, and propagate differentiated
image bounds through the logarithm.  These estimates combine into a global
three-chart theorem on the full class interval.

The antipode is treated as a Morse--Bott cut point: the two shortest radial
image terms encode an $S^2$-family of minimizing geodesics and give
$p_t(\pi)\asymp t^{-5/2}e^{-\pi^2/(2t)}$.  Exact normalization also yields a
Haar-probability tail bound.  A rational validation record instantiates
orders zero through eight at $t_0=1/5$ and records the positivity margins and
all derivative orders using exact integer comparisons.  In lattice
normalization the estimates give explicit weak-field, convexity, and
nonlinear-remainder bounds for a plaquette action.  They do not establish an
interacting-measure estimate, a renormalization-group trajectory, continuum
Yang--Mills theory, confinement, or a mass gap.
\end{abstract}
